metadata.title: Jalen Nailor Sidelined with a Concussion to Open Practice Week
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not practice on Wednesday as the team begins to prepare for Week 5 against the New England Patriots, according to Anthony Galaviz of The Fresno Bee. Nailor initially suffered the injury in Sunday's loss to the Chiefs, and it forced him to miss part of the game. Now, he's at risk of missing all of next week's game against the Patriots if he doesn't clear concussion protocol in time. It's not often that players are able to clear the protocol in seven days, but it's not impossible. Fantasy managers should monitor the Raiders' practice reports going forward, especially when they release their game status designations on Friday. If Nailor can't suit up this week, Tre Tucker and Cody White would step into larger roles in the passing game.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor (concussion) misses practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Jalen Nailor (concussion) missed Las Vegas' practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: Nailor left Sunday's game early after suffering a concussion and has since entered the NFL's concussion protocols. He wasn't able to practice on Wednesday as a result, and it looks like it will be a real threat to his availability for Week 5. Look for Tre Tucker and Cody White to see more opportunities if the veteran misses any time.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor - Absent for practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said that Nailor (concussion) won't practice Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
metadata.analysis: Nailor entered the NFL's concussion protocol after exiting Sunday's loss to the Chiefs due to the head injury. If he's unable to gain clearance to play Week 5 against the Patriots, Tre Tucker and Cody White would likely serve as the Raiders' top two receivers. Dont'e Thornton (hamstring) remains on injured reserve, but he could also be an option at wideout this Sunday after the Raiders opened 21-day practice window Wednesday.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor leaves Week 4 with a concussion
metadata.description: Jalen Nailor was not targeted in a 30-27 loss to the Chiefs in Week 4.
metadata.analysis: Nailor suffered a concussion during the first half and did not return. He will now enter the league's concussion protocol as he attempts to get cleared in time for a Week 5 matchup against the Patriots.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor - Suffers concussion Sunday
metadata.description: Nailor (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's contest against the Chiefs.
metadata.analysis: Nailor took a blow to the head late in the second quarter, and he was ultimately diagnosed with a concussion. The wide receiver will finish his day having recorded no stats. In his absence, Tre Tucker, Cody White and Dareke Young will operate as the Raiders' top options at wide receiver.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor Ruled Out with a Concussion
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Jalen Nailor (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's contest against the Kansas City Chiefs with a concussion. Nailor did not draw a single target before sustaining the injury. Since catching three passes in Week 1, Nailor has brought in only two passes for a mere 25 yards. For the remainder of the contest, Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer, and Tre Tucker should operate as the top options for Kirk Cousins.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor Likely Off The Fantasy Radar in Week 4 Matchup vs. Chiefs
metadata.description: While Jalen Nailor operates as the No. 2 wide receiver on the depth chart for the Las Vegas Raiders, he has not yet provided any true value in fantasy football. Nailor, who has played 119 offensive snaps across three games, has totaled just five receptions (on 11 targets) for 52 yards (10.4 yards per catch) and zero touchdowns. It doesn't get any easier in Week 4, as Nailor faces a Kansas City Chiefs defense that ranks sixth in the NFL in passing yards per game allowed (178.3). With the recent return of tight end Brock Bowers, and with additional competition in the passing game from running back Ashton Jeanty (who leads the team in receptions with 13), wide receiver Tre Tucker (who leads the Raiders in receiving yards with 189) and tight end Michael Mayer, Nailor's targets remain a question mark. Nailor is currently rostered in just 8% of Yahoo leagues and is off the radar as RotoBaller's No. 77 wide receiver in Week 4. He can safely remain out of lineups this week.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor - Three targets in win
metadata.description: Nailor caught one of his three targets for 16 yards in the Raiders' 35-27 win over the Saints on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Nailor struggled for the Raiders in Week 3. The team relied more on tight end Brock Bowers to carry the receiving offense. Tre Tucker and Nailor received over three times fewer targets than the tight end in the contest, with Bowers establishing the pecking order early in his return from injury.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor catches one pass Sunday
metadata.description: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Nailor remains uninvolved in the offense with Las Vegas. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor Better Left on Benches in Week 3
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Jalen Nailor has not done enough through two weeks to make himself a comfortable Week 3 option against New Orleans. Nailor has four catches for 36 yards on eight targets, and he played only 60% of the offensive snaps in each of the first two games. He is still listed as a starter opposite Tre Tucker, but the role has not produced much. Brock Bowers is also questionable after missing Friday's practice, and his return would add another target to an offense that already has several mouths to feed. The matchup itself is workable, with New Orleans allowing 204 passing yards per game through two weeks. Nailor sits at WR71 in RotoBaller's latest Week 3 rankings, which fits how difficult he is to trust right now. Unless the Raiders suddenly lean on him more heavily, Nailor belongs on fantasy benches in most leagues this week.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor Playing Limited Role in Raiders Passing Game
metadata.description: Entering his first season with the Las Vegas Raiders in 2026, veteran wide receiver Jalen Nailor appeared to be in the best position of his career to play a featured role in his team's passing game. However, the 27-year-old has recorded just four catches for 36 yards on eight targets across the Raiders' first two games of the year. While Nailor profiles as the WR2 in Las Vegas alongside WR1 Tre Tucker, he played just 60% of his team's offensive snaps in both Week 1 and Week 2. With star Raiders tight end Brock Bowers (knee) nearing a return from knee surgery, Nailor's role in the Las Vegas passing game could shrink even further in the weeks to come. Heading into Week 3, Nailor should be off the radar of fantasy managers in the majority of league formats.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor quiet in win Sunday
metadata.description: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-3 targets for nine yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
metadata.analysis: Nailor was a non-factor on Sunday. He caught just one pass against the Chargers and wasn't able to do much of note with it. He isn't expected to be a good fantasy option moving forward, especially with Brock Bowers (knee) set to return to the lineup in the very near future.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor - Pedestrian performance in Week 2
metadata.description: Nailor caught one of three targets for nine yards in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Chargers.
metadata.analysis: Nailor's three targets were fourth on the team, and he continues to run plenty of routes. The production is lacking through two games, as Nailor has just four catches for 36 scoreless yards on eight targets. Cody White secured a pair of touchdowns as the fourth wideout Sunday, and it will be interesting to see if White starts getting more snaps at Nailor or Jack Bech's expense.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor Not Worth the Risk vs. Chargers in Week 2
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Jalen Nailor has to leap off the stat sheet in Week 2 against the Los Angeles Chargers after an almost non-existent start to the season. The former Minnesota Viking entered the 2026 season with plenty of fanfare after signing a three-year, $35 million contract in the offseason. However, he was stymied in the season opener against the Miami Dolphins, catching three of five passes for just 27 yards. The game plan didn't help Nailor's case in Week 1, with Las Vegas leaning on the run game and new starting quarterback Kirk Cousins preferring short passes to running back Ashton Jeanty and targeting young receiver Jack Bech. Plus, the door hasn't completely closed on Nailor yet since Brock Bowers' (knee) absence for a second straight week could lead to more targets. While things could turn around for Nailor, fantasy managers should sit him until he shows legitimate production.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor Not Living Up to His Paycheck
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Jalen Nailor made his team debut in Week 1, but it resulted in just three catches for 27 yards. Considering that the Raiders paid him $35 million this past offseason, we would have expected the ex-Viking to have a bigger role with his new team. It's not like he faced much competition, either. Instead, he was losing targets to players with less experience, such as Tre Tucker and Jack Bech. It's possible that Week 1 was a fluke, especially since the Raiders naturally went run-heavy against an inferior Dolphins team. However, we'd need to see him maintain fantasy relevance before we can trust him in lineups. His next opportunity to get back on track will be Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers. He should be benched in most leagues for now.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor - Three catches in Las Vegas debut
metadata.description: Nailor caught three passes on five targets for 27 yards during the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Nailor ended up leading all Raiders wide receivers in targets, though he finished third in that category behind Michael Mayer (seven) and running back Ashton Jeanty (six). Even with Brock Bowers (knee) sidelined, it looks like Nailor will operate in a complementary role in the Raiders' offense, especially in games where Jeanty gets it going as he did against Miami. Things won't get easier for Nailor in Week 2 against a 49ers defense that held Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and the rest of the Rams pass catchers in check in a 27-7 Week 1 win for San Francisco.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor catches three passes in Week 1
metadata.description: Jalen Nailor caught three of his five targets for 27 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1.
metadata.analysis: Nailor was one of many that saw involvement in the Las Vegas passing offense, finishing as one of six to catch at least one pass in the win. The wideout will look to offer more impactful potential in a revamped Las Vegas offense as the season moves forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor Offers Flex Value in Week 1
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Jalen Nailor is ready to make his team debut against the Miami Dolphins in Week 1. After four years with the Minnesota Vikings, Nailor signed a three-year deal with the Raiders this past offseason. He'll now get a chance to establish himself as a top target in an offense after being stuck behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison in Minnesota. Nailor could see an uptick in workload with tight end Brock Bowers (knee) being unavailable for this game. Both Nailor and quarterback Kirk Cousins are new to this organization, so it could take time to build chemistry. Fantasy managers should be able to put in Nailor as a flex option for this weekend, but don't expect much more than that.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor's Opportunity Makes Him a Late-Round Sleeper
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Jalen Nailor has a much cleaner path to volume than he ever had in Minnesota. Nailor spent four years buried behind Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, but he enters 2026 listed with the first-team offense in a wide receiver room that doesn't have an established target hog. He caught 29 of 53 targets for 444 yards and four touchdowns last season, then spent August building real chemistry with Kirk Cousins. Nailor caught a deep score from Cousins on Aug. 6, another touchdown on Aug. 10 and two more in red-zone work a week later. That doesn't guarantee a huge target share, especially with Brock Bowers likely to remain the centerpiece and Tre Tucker and Jack Bech still involved. It does give Nailor a legitimate chance to see more work than he ever did with the Vikings. Las Vegas signed him early in free agency, kept him with the starters all summer, and the opportunity held through roster cuts. For managers looking for a late-round receiver with room to beat his draft cost, Nailor has a pretty easy case to make.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor - Two catches in preseason loss
metadata.description: Nailor brought in two of four targets for 13 yards in the Raiders' 18-12 preseason loss to the 49ers on Thursday.
metadata.analysis: Nailor led the Raiders in targets and finished tied for second in receptions. The fifth-year pro made his first catch on a pass from Kirk Cousins for a seven-yard gain during the opening possession, and he recorded his second and final one with Fernando Mendoza under center to open Las Vegas' third drive. Nailor was then also the intended target deep down the middle on the next play, a pass that resulted in an interception. Nailor is projected to open the regular season as the No. 2 receiver and posted a 3-35-0 line on seven targets in two preseason games.

metadata.title: Jalen Nailor Making a Case for Late-Round Value
metadata.description: Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Jalen Nailor has strengthened his late-round redraft case by holding onto a starting job throughout August. Nailor signed a three-year, $35.03 million deal with Las Vegas after setting career highs with 29 catches and 444 receiving yards to go with four touchdowns in 2025, and the Raiders still list him with the first-team offense. His chemistry with Kirk Cousins has also shown up repeatedly in camp. Nailor caught a deep touchdown from Cousins on August 6, another score during red-zone work on August 10, and two more touchdowns from him in the red zone on August 17. He then caught one of three targets for 22 yards against Houston while playing into the third drive. There is still some risk here. Head coach Klint Kubiak recently challenged the entire receiver room to be more consistent, while Brock Bowers should remain the focal point of the passing game and Tre Tucker and Jack Bech will compete for targets. Still, Nailor's starting role, vertical ability, and repeated red-zone production have made him more interesting than he was entering camp. RotoBaller currently has him at WR64.
